verdict.rationale: Proa compiles components through a macro that validates templates at compile time and consolidates static markup. For interactive islands, adding signals and event handlers makes Proa emit the needed JavaScript as a small vanilla-JS module on a roughly 1.3 KB runtime. That points to compiler-generated, signal-driven client updates, but the evidence never says these modules perform targeted DOM patching rather than re-rendering, and most of the compile-time work described targets server HTML output. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that island JS performs surgical DOM updates without diffing, details of how signals map to DOM mutations, independent or hands-on corroboration.
